answer: A sealed-replica deposit forces each agent key to rent its own disk. On joining, a key encodes a public 64 GB archive, such as falcon tracking data, into a replica sealed with its address, so clones cannot share one copy, and it locks 20 POA. Each epoch the chain names 10 random chunks to return within 2 seconds, faster than any re-encoding can run. One agent stores 64 GB once; 1,000 fakes need 64 TB online plus 20,000 POA, a bill that hits its zenith as the farm grows. Three missed checks burn the deposit and mark the key sable, barred from pay. Weakness: rich farms can still buy disks.
